title: Knowledge Compiler: Structured Knowledge Extraction from Textbooks
oneLiner: Structured evidence infrastructure with partial provenance recovery over a historical textbook-derived corpus.
keyTakeaways: The historical inventory contains 2,305 files—707 from ACSM and 1,598 from NSCA—representing 2,294 unique IDs.

A provenance-recovery audit identifies 571 strongest-subset records and quarantines 1,734 records from unsupported reuse. Automated checks enforce structural constraints but do not establish factual accuracy or scientific validity.
The pipeline was applied to two exercise-science textbooks; this is implementation reuse within one domain, not evidence of scientific transfer.
The pipeline is designed to be source-extensible; cross-domain generalization has not been tested.
Pipeline cost: ~$0.003 per object using structured LLM extraction with schema enforcement.

faq.q: Why compile textbooks into structured knowledge?
faq.a: Structured records expose stored source locators to downstream systems. The recovered subset supports re-checkable source relations, not ground-truth status, factual correctness, or scientific admissibility.

The public artifact currently documents 13 Knowledge IR node types, including concepts, thresholds, recommendations, procedures, warnings, evidence, formulas, figures, and supporting table and decision types.

faq.q: Can this pipeline work for other textbooks?
faq.a: The pipeline has been applied to ACSM and NSCA exercise-science textbooks. This supports transfer across two sources within one domain; cross-domain generalization has not been tested.
